name: amtterm
why: A door into Intel AMT serial-over-LAN, a management channel hiding inside many business machines that few people ever examine.

brief.what_it_is: amtterm is a serial-over-LAN (SOL) client for Intel AMT, the out-of-band management feature in some Intel-based machines. According to the homepage, it ships as a terminal program and a graphical GTK version. The page also says it comes with a Perl script that gathers information about AMT-managed computers and remotely controls them. The homepage does not say what credentials or network setup the client needs, or the exact input and output formats.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no stated motivation. It only describes what the tools are.
brief.install_notes: The homepage does not describe installation, dependencies, or configuration. It links to a git repository and to release tarballs, with tarballs split into versions 1.8 and later and versions 1.7 and earlier. I did not follow those links because their URLs were not given in the page text. The Homebrew formula lists four executables: amtider, amtterm, amttool, and gamt.
brief.standout: The page describes a terminal client and a GTK client in one package, plus a Perl script for information gathering and remote control, so it covers more than a single console session. The scout note calls AMT a management channel hidden in many business machines; the homepage itself does not say that.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage shows no release dates, last-commit dates, or maintenance notes, and I did not reach the git repository or release pages to check them.
brief.caveats: The homepage is a short blurb with no usage examples, no command lines, and no description of supported hardware or AMT versions. The Homebrew formula has no caveats. Working with AMT normally requires access to the managed machine's management interface, which the page does not explain. The page does not state a license.
quotes: This is a serial-over-lan (sol) client for Intel AMT.
Includes a terminal and a graphical (gtk) version.
Also comes with a perl script to gather informations about and remotely control AMT managed computers.
fetch_log: https://www.kraxel.org/blog/linux/amtterm/ — fetched OK; short page with description and links to git repository and release tarballs (no URLs given in the text). Did not follow further links.
